chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Armstrong's funeral and his own
summary: He was too sick to see Armstrong's funeral; asked about his own, he says only to give him another drink.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Speaking of Louis Armstrong, did you see his funeral on TV?
No, I didn't see it. I was too sick to look.

Peggy Lee sang The Lord's Prayer and there were a couple of other things like that, but he didn't have the New Orleans type of funeral... Do you think that he would have like to have had a New Orleans type funeral? Did he ever talk about the type of funeral that he might like?
I haven't heard of it, nothing.
Well, just from your knowing him, what kind of funeral do you think he would have -
Just by knowing him, the only thing I can say is he was just the greatest guy and he should have had one of the best funerals.
What would you consider to be a best funeral?
Just another funeral.
I mean like we have always had - when I say we I mean black people, we've always had, especially black musicians -
Color don't make no difference.
No, but I mean the musicians have had different types of funerals.
People like could go to the funeral and could get in ... and watch the casket go by, something like that.
How about the bands that played?
I figured they might have a band from New Orleans to play for him. But I don't know because I think I just came out of the hospital the day before or after. We were in the hospital the same time.
Have you ever thought about what you would like to have the musicians do in tribute to you?
No, hm-mm. Just say, well, he was a pretty good old guy. (LAUGHTER)
Tell me, how would like to be remembered?
And give him another drink! (LAUGHTER)... I don't know what's going to happen to me when I'm dead.
What would you like to see happen to you? Would you like to have one of your favorite musicians play a specific song for you or something?
No, no.
Would you like some of your music played at your funeral?

Well, that's kind of tough to talk about. I've been dreaming I was dying for the past two weeks... I mean that's the kind of pills the doctors give me, you know, hallucinations, you have everything like that, you know.
